BATCH C · BOARD 5 OF 6

Two flows

Both are measured against one number: time-to-first-actionable-answer — the moment Alex can change what she does at the bench, not the moment someone replies. Elapsed time is annotated cumulatively at every step, with the fork where the flow either resolves in hours or waits two days.

8METHOD CARD
permanent
Versioned, forkable, DOI-bearing, with the failure condition recorded. The next person with this problem never reaches step 1 — retrieval hands them this at step 2.
F11 F12 F14 F15
THE CLOCK, HONESTLY
retrieval resolves it at step 20 m
answered same day · target6 h 27 m
routed at 48 h, then answered≈ 55 h
Alex's stated need is "before I repeat the same failure for another week". A week is 168 hours; every branch here beats it, and the point of the design is to move mass from the yellow bar to the green one.
WHERE THE TIME ACTUALLY GOES
Of 6 h 27 m, Alex spends 7 minutes and the platform spends 6 h 20 m waiting for a human. Nothing in the composer is worth optimising further; everything in routing, notification and the size of the answering pool is.
WHAT THE ORDER 5 → 4 MEANS
The ribbon is drawn through screen 5 because that is the path we must design for, not the one we hope for. In the happy case the flow skips 5 entirely and 4 arrives on the same day. Both are shown so nobody presents the happy path as the typical one.
FLOW B

Negative result becomes a reusable object

12 → 13 · the flow no existing venue closes
12POST · SIX FIELDS
≈ 12 mfrom data already in hand
Hypothesis, method (a card, not prose), conditions, what happened, what it rules out, confidence. Twelve minutes because the run is already recorded — the six fields are a re-framing, not new work.
The copy never uses the word failure about the researcher. Orange, never red.
F14 F11 F12 B15
13REUSE COUNTER
days → months
"This saved 4 labs from repeating it." The counter is the whole reason the loop closes: it is the first time anyone has told a researcher what their null result was worth, in a unit they care about.
Plus a DOI, a citation, a place in the failure taxonomy, an attachment on MC-0288, and +12 on the Replication axis.
F14 F15 B13 B14 B15
ΣTHE 71% / 0% PROBLEM
71%
WOULD SUBMIT A
NEGATIVE RESULT
0%
FOLLOW AN EXISTING
NEGATIVE-RESULTS VENUE
Willingness was never the constraint. The gap is a destination people already visit. So this flow has no separate venue, no separate submission, no separate audience: the null result lives on the method card that produced it, in the taxonomy people browse when stuck, and in the retrieval panel of the next person to type the same question.
The two-step flow is the design. A third step would be a submission process, and a submission process is what the 0% already ignore.
